foz2i9: This week you review three classes: the plural of a group of words, adjectives that agree and the position of the adjective. Here you see it with objects from a craft market, step by step, so you can study on your own.
czhl85: You already know how to make a noun plural. Now look at the **whole group**: article or number + noun + adjective. If there are several things, all three words change: _una vela verde → tres velas verdes_.
plc321: Numbers don't change (_dos, tres, cuatro…_). From **dos** on, the noun and the adjective are plural. The adjective follows the same rule as the noun: vowel + **-s** (_rojas_), consonant + **-es** (_azules_), **-z → -ces** (_felices_).
1n5ull0: Two special cases: words in **-ión** lose the written accent (_una reunión larga → dos reuniones largas_), and weekdays ending in **-s** don't change, only the article does: _el lunes → los lunes_.
og7m32: After you write a plural, run your finger along the group: do all the words end in **-s**?
2bgd2w: The adjective becomes plural too: consonant + **-es**.
17ze9zv: In the plural, _reuniones_ has no written accent.
1pxggzz: The adjective says what something is like: its colour, its size, its origin. It always **agrees** with the noun: masculine or feminine, singular or plural.
1pv65ob: Adjectives in **-o** have **four forms**: _negro, negra, negros, negras_. Adjectives in **-e** or a consonant have **two forms**, one for singular and one for plural: _verde, verdes_; _azul, azules_; _feliz, felices_.
1wbz83a: Nationalities ending in a consonant do change for the feminine: _español → española_, _alemán → alemana_, _inglés → inglesa_. Notice: in the feminine the written accent disappears. And they are written in lower case.
1jeprqk: If the group mixes masculine and feminine, the adjective is **masculine plural**: _un vaso y una jarra rojos_.
1op50f9: _Blusa_ is feminine: the adjective ends in **-a**.
4sxrjv: In the feminine, _inglesa_ has no written accent.
1php1dt: After to describe, before to give an opinion
1tybbq6: The normal order in Spanish is **noun + adjective**: _una casa amarilla_, _un mercado grande_, _un café mexicano_. This is how you describe: colour, shape, size, origin. Always after.
1gbe693: A few adjectives go **before** when you give your **opinion**: _un buen café_, _una mala noche_, _una gran ciudad_. Before a masculine singular noun, **bueno** and **malo** get shorter: _buen_, _mal_. **Grande** becomes **gran** before any singular noun, masculine or feminine.
1erg1fp: In the plural there is no short form: _buenos amigos_, _grandes ideas_. And after _es_ or _son_, the adjective is complete: _El café es bueno_.
xllc17: Colour describes: it goes **after** the noun.
5it6fd: With some adjectives, the position changes what you say. **After** the noun they have the basic meaning; **before**, another meaning.
1geovn8: _Una ciudad grande_ has a lot of inhabitants; _una gran ciudad_ is important or impressive. _Un compañero viejo_ is old in years; _un viejo compañero_ is a colleague from a long time ago. _Una bici nueva_ has just been bought; _una nueva bici_ is another bike, different from the previous one. _Un sombrero único_ is very special; _el único sombrero_ is the only one, there is no other.
9jbn4g: For a person's age, _viejo_ can sound harsh: it is kinder to say **mayor**: _una señora mayor_.
9kotlz: If in doubt, put the adjective **after**: it is almost always correct and has the basic meaning.
1yjqmr2: For a person's age, the kind word is **mayor**; _vieja_ before the noun changes the meaning.

1u8xwss: Spanish has two **r** sounds. The **soft r** is a very short tap of the tongue, like the _tt_ in American English _better_: _caro_, _claro_, _negro_, _amarillo_, _para_.
aoj3yr: The **strong r** is a long trill: the tongue vibrates several times. It is written **rr** between vowels (_carro_, _barro_, _jarra_) and **r** at the start of a word (_rojo_, _regalo_, _rebozo_).
1ov2y4q: Careful: changing the sound changes the word. _Caro_ (a lot of money) is not _carro_ (car); _pero_ is not _perro_.
mm2uu5: Between vowels, one **r** sounds soft and two (**rr**) sound strong. At the start of a word you write a single **r**, but it sounds strong: _rojo_, never _rrojo_.
1koesev: Both **r** sounds at the start are strong: re-, ro-.
1upw56f: Strong **rr** in _jarras_ and _barro_; soft in _negro_ and _tres_.
